guards.kind: browser (playwright + real WebGL2 via SwiftShader). Drives window.__fractalRenderer directly; three deep-zoom views, each rendered twice (LA on / LA off). The only guard in the repo asserting ADR-0065/0066 glitch-freedom.

Reproduced identically on a second clean run — the numbers are deterministic.
guards.exitContractNote: fail() prints and process.exit(1) immediately — first failure aborts, so a red run names exactly one view and one assertion. Sound, but it means an early view's failure hides the later two.
guards.break: Two breaks, applied and reverted independently with targeted Edits. (A) engine/fractal/deepZoom/referenceOrbit.ts — the auto-reference gate inverted, `built.escaped` -> `!built.escaped` (grep disableAutoReference). This reproduces bug 1 from the guard's own header exactly: orbitLen fell to 588, the number the header names. (C) engine/fractal/shaders/fractalDisplay.ts — `texture(uImage, vUv).rgb` -> a constant colour, i.e. a completely blank render with the CPU-side deep-zoom build untouched.
guards.result: (A) RED, exit 1, 44-50s: 'auto-reference did not relocate'. But its dominant went 0.019 -> 0.500/0.599 while DELTA WAS ONLY 0.099 (0.112 on the repeat) — under the 0.18 bound. The square detector did not catch the glitch it was written for; the relocated assertion did. (C) **GREEN, exit 0, 18 min, all three views 1.000/1.000 d=0.000**, full success banner 'glitch-free ... all match the pure-PO baseline' — with nothing rendered at all. After repair: (C) RED at view 1 in 52s, (A) RED at view 1 in 44s, both on the new ceiling.
guards.verdict: DEFECTIVE — the detector is relative and cancels any defect shared by both captures; repaired additively and re-falsified two ways
guards.note: Lesson 1 in its purest form: 'the render changed' and 'the render is blank' both satisfy |dominant_on - dominant_off| < 0.18. The relative comparison is blind to the entire reference-orbit / auto-reference / nucleus half of ADR-0065/0066, because that half is shared by both captures. Fifth-failure-mode check: the three views are inline so the matrix cannot shrink; a missing __fractalRenderer throws inside page.evaluate and a missing canvas returns -1 and fails — both prove their subject exists.

findings.summary: Residual after the repair: the smoke's outcome still depends on how many RAF frames land inside its fixed 1200ms settle window, and that varies run to run.
findings.rationale: CLAIM: the fixed `waitForTimeout(1200)` is a proxy for 'enough frames to reach the wall and reflect'. EVIDENCE: across 22 runs in this batch, healthy max-penetration ranged 0.0023-0.0111 and the WALL_THRESHOLD=99 break reached only 0.0320 where the bounce-disabled break reached 0.0971-0.1144 — same break, different frame counts. The penetration bound has enough margin that this no longer flips the verdict (5/5 and 4/4 clean), but the underlying variance is still there. OPTIONS: (a) leave it — the margin is now ~4x either way and it has not flipped since the repair; (b) replace the fixed wait with a poll on a frame counter, the way smoke:liquify was hardened in batch 4, so the window is measured in frames rather than milliseconds; (c) drive the particle step deterministically from the test instead of riding the RAF loop. RECOMMENDATION: (b) if this ever goes red without an obvious cause; not worth doing pre-emptively, but worth knowing before anyone calls a future red 'flake'.

findings.summary: The dead IS_COMPILING listener block is annotated @stale in place rather than removed, because removal is the owner's call.
findings.rationale: CLAIM: the block sets __compileSeen = false, tries to attach a listener via window.FractalEvents, and nothing ever reads the flag. EVIDENCE: a scratch probe against fractal-toy.html read window.FractalEvents and window.__fractalEvents as undefined, and __compileSeen as false after a switch that demonstrably happened (formula went to Mandelbox). OPTIONS: (a) delete the block — it is five lines of provable no-op; (b) leave the @stale annotation, which is what was done; (c) expose FractalEvents on window in the fractal-toy entry and make the listener real, which would add a genuine second proof of the rebuild alongside the uniform swap. RECOMMENDATION: (a) is safe and (c) is the only one that adds coverage; either is a two-minute change, but both are deletions or product edits made for a test's benefit, so neither was done unattended.

summary.headline: All eight were defective — the first batch in this sweep with no healthy guard in it, and the failures cluster: SEVEN of the eight had at least one assertion that a vanished, blank, or zeroed subject satisfied. smoke:gx-fractal-glitch printed its full 'deep-zoom LA path is glitch-free' banner at exit 0 on a completely blank render, and its 0.18 delta bound turned out looser than the very glitch its header names (measured 0.099). smoke:bc-drag declared '✓ defaults: brush.size=0.15' having just printed a defaults object with no brushSize in it. smoke:particle-bounce passed 5 runs in 6 with bouncing disabled. smoke:fractal-kind covered one of the four contracts it listed and named the wrong owner for that one.

summary.notesForNextBatch: Two patterns worth carrying forward. (1) A wrong break is common in browser smokes because store values have several writers — renaming the slice default for sampleCap, and for julia.kind, both failed to move the observed value; fluid-toy overrides one at boot and the view-library seed writes the other. When a break does not land, probe the value's provenance before concluding the guard is blind. (2) Two of the eight defects were only visible after PRINTING the discriminating quantity — particle penetration and the demo.size swing. Instrumenting the guard with a temporary MEASURE line, running it 5x healthy and 5x broken, and only then choosing a bound, cost about four minutes each time and produced thresholds with 4x margin instead of guesses.
